title: Frequency-addressed modal cell: the field as compressed computational matter
summary: This pass records a cross-family synthesis that only became explicit after the resonance, field-computing, computational-matter, NSSN and structural-compiler lines were viewed together. Earlier projects mostly chose a wave/field substrate and asked what it could compute. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell reverses that direction: start from an already-interesting resonant, state-dependent receiver and ask what smaller operator description survives compression. v0 shows that state compression is not mechanism compression: rank-8 POD captures 99.86% of a 36-state teacher while naive nonlinear closure fails autonomous rollout. v1 extends the object through branching axonal matter with deliberately weak local ephaptic timing. v2 then supplies the boring attacker: frozen axonal branching collapses exactly to a nine-edge sparse graph with fixed delays; only the context-dependent timing perturbation remains outside that fixed-delay abstraction. The sharper wall lesson is therefore that spatial matter earns computational status only through runtime-dependent state/operator effects, not merely because its geometry is complicated.

nodes.claim: Tests whether rich receiving and transmitting matter can be reduced to cheaper executable operators while preserving the runtime-dependent computation that survives boring graph, resonator and reduced-state attackers.
nodes.survived: v0 establishes strong state compressibility (rank-8 POD energy 0.998602) and some locally learnable nonlinear transition structure. v1 adds grown branching axonal routes and a weak local coactivity-dependent timing perturbation: nearby synchronous bundles shift mean conduction delay by 1.473% (0.165 rad mean arrival-phase shift at omega=0.42), while spatial separation and temporal staggering suppress the effect by >98%. v2 then shows the fixed-delay graph attacker misses the near synchronous context by 0.40235 step RMS / 0.16899 rad RMS while matching the uncoupled arbor exactly.
nodes.killed: The naive nonlinear modal closure from v0 fails autonomous held-out rollout, so low-dimensional state geometry does not itself yield a stable computational law. v2 additionally kills any stronger claim that branching axonal geometry alone is a new computational primitive: the frozen arbor is exactly reducible to a sparse graph with one fixed delay per terminal route. Even the surviving ephaptic timing residue is not irreducible; a conventional graph with activity-dependent delays could emulate it. The result is a decomposition boundary, not proof of a new neuron architecture.

edges.why: The new repository explicitly builds its teacher from the NotSoSimpleNeuron quasi-active frequency gate plus the later synthetic local voltage-dependent interaction, then asks whether those resident state-conditioned dynamics admit a much smaller autonomous modal surrogate.

Entrain already made frequency an executable routing coordinate and measured its Arnold-tongue resolution limit. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell keeps frequency/phase as the probe address but changes the scientific direction from constructing oscillator matter to reducing an existing richer receiver.

InformationFlow demonstrated WHERE/WHICH/SIGN selection through spatial overlap, frequency and phase but supplied its useful nonlinear coupling explicitly. The new reduction experiment asks whether useful state-dependent coupling can instead be extracted from richer computational matter rather than written into the field law by hand.

Operaattori shows the forward reduction idea on real morphology: complicated physical structure can compile to compact transport and nonlinear operator objects. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell applies the analogous compression question to a resonant state-dependent synthetic receiver, without claiming direct ancestry or that the v0 teacher is Operaattori's biological model.

motifs.title: The field is no longer the hypothesis; it is a reduced representation of computational matter
motifs.description: Earlier field and oscillator projects usually started by choosing a field law and exploring the computation it could support. Operaattori, NotSoSimpleNeuron and FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell point in the reverse direction: begin with a richer physical or synthetic receiver, identify what operator family it actually implements, and try to compress that family into a smaller executable object. The v0 failure sharpens the rule: a compact state manifold is not enough; the reduced law must remain causal and stable when run autonomously on interventions it did not fit.

motifs.title: Frequency can address a resident operator, but filtering alone is not enough
motifs.description: SpectralNeuron establishes the boring floor: resonance supplies finite FDM-style addressing. Entrain adds measured entrainment routing and phase relations. InformationFlow uses frequency/phase/spatial overlap to select a nonlinear write. NotSoSimpleNeuron then shows the stronger receiver-side object: active resident state changes cross-mode coupling and the operator encountered by the next event. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell asks whether that stronger object can be compressed while keeping frequency/phase as the external address rather than confusing a band-pass filter with the computation itself.

motifs.title: A compressed representation earns mechanism status only when it survives new interventions
motifs.description: MatrixInMatrix already separates a compact harmonic reconstruction from the source dynamics that heal and evolve. NeuralAlgorithmDecoding requires an executable causal surrogate rather than a pretty hidden geometry. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell makes the same boundary dynamical: rank-8 coordinates explain almost all sampled state variance, yet a locally better nonlinear transition fit fails when autonomously rolled through unseen frequencies, tone pairs and histories. Representation compression and mechanism compression are different gates.

motifs.title: Frozen structure can collapse to a graph; runtime-dependent matter is the surviving residue
motifs.description: The axonal extension creates a useful correction to the structure-as-computation story. Development can manufacture a branching route, but once that geometry is frozen and conduction is context-free, a sparse graph with fixed delays reproduces terminal arrival timing exactly. What survives the attacker is not branching itself but the weak dependence of propagation timing on nearby co-active axonal matter. This keeps the claim narrow: physical structure may determine the operator, while runtime material state determines whether the operator is richer than a static graph representation.
